items.q: A 48-year-old patient with an expanding pituitary macroadenoma undergoes automated perimetry. What characteristic visual field deficit is expected?
items.exp: Pituitary adenomas expand upward from the sella, compressing the decussating nasal retinal axons in the optic chiasm, leading to loss of both temporal visual fields (bitemporal hemianopia).
r: Correct. Compression of decussating nasal retinal fibers causes bitemporal hemianopia.
Incorrect. Right optic tract lesion causes left homonymous hemianopia.
Incorrect. Temporal lobe lesion damaging Meyer loop causes superior quadrantanopia.
Incorrect. Monocular blindness requires pre-chiasmatic optic nerve damage.
items.kp: Chiasmal compression by pituitary tumors damages crossing nasal retinal fibers, causing bitemporal hemianopia.

items.q: Surgical resection of a right anterior temporal lobe seizure focus injures Meyer loop. Which visual field defect will the patient manifest postoperatively?
o: Left superior quadrantanopia (pie in the sky)
Left inferior quadrantanopia (pie on the floor)
items.exp: Meyer loop fibers represent the inferior retina (superior visual field) and course through the temporal lobe. Right-sided injury produces contralateral superior quadrantanopia (pie in the sky).
r: Correct. Right Meyer loop damage causes contralateral superior quadrantanopia (pie in the sky).
Incorrect. Inferior quadrantanopia results from parietal optic radiation damage.
Incorrect. Complete hemianopia requires complete tract or radiation destruction.
Incorrect. Bitemporal defect occurs only at the chiasm.
items.kp: Temporal lobe lesions damaging Meyer loop produce contralateral superior quadrantanopia (pie in the sky).

items.q: A 70-year-old patient with an acute left posterior cerebral artery stroke exhibits right homonymous hemianopia. On formal testing, central high-acuity foveal vision is completely preserved. What explains this macular sparing?
o: Dual collateral blood supply from middle cerebral artery branches
Bilateral projection of foveal photoreceptors at the optic chiasm
Direct innervation of fovea from frontal eye fields
items.exp: Macular sparing occurs in PCA cortical strokes because the occipital pole representing the macula receives rich collateral arterial flow from terminal branches of the middle cerebral artery.
r: Correct. Collateral flow from terminal branches of the middle cerebral artery preserves occipital pole perfusion.
Incorrect. Retinal projections do not duplicate foveal representations across the chiasm.
Incorrect. Frontal eye fields control voluntary saccades, not sensory visual perception.
Incorrect. The lesion is in the occipital cortex, not the chiasm.
items.kp: Macular sparing in posterior cerebral artery strokes is due to collateral perfusion from middle cerebral artery terminal branches.

items.q: Third-order sensory neurons in the primary visual pathway project their axons from which thalamic nucleus to the calcarine visual cortex?
items.exp: Axons in the optic tract synapse in the lateral geniculate nucleus (LGN) of the thalamus. LGN neurons project as the optic radiations to the calcarine cortex.
r: Correct. The lateral geniculate nucleus relays visual sensory input to the primary visual cortex.
Incorrect. Medial geniculate nucleus relays auditory signals.
Incorrect. VPL relays somatic sensory signals from the body.
Incorrect. VPM relays facial sensation and taste.
items.kp: The lateral geniculate nucleus of the thalamus is the primary relay station for visual pathways.

items.q: Complete transection of the left optic tract results in which visual field defect?
items.exp: The left optic tract carries axons from the left temporal hemiretina and right nasal hemiretina, representing the entire right visual hemifield. A lesion produces complete right homonymous hemianopia.
r: Correct. Left optic tract destruction abolishes perception of the entire right visual hemifield.
Incorrect. Left hemianopia requires a right retrochiasmal lesion.
Incorrect. Bitemporal hemianopia requires central chiasm compression.
Incorrect. Monocular left eye blindness requires left optic nerve transection.
items.kp: Lesions of the optic tract or complete retrochiasmal pathway cause contralateral homonymous hemianopia.

items.q: Which visual pathway fibers traverse the parietal lobe optic radiation (Baum loop)?
o: Superior retinal fibers representing the inferior visual field
Inferior retinal fibers representing the superior visual field
Fibers from the fovea centralis only
items.exp: The parietal optic radiations carry fibers from the superior retina (representing the inferior visual field). Lesions here produce a contralateral inferior quadrantanopia (pie on the floor).
r: Correct. Parietal radiations carry superior retinal fibers representing the lower visual field.
Incorrect. Inferior retinal fibers loop through the temporal lobe (Meyer loop).
Incorrect. Foveal fibers project across both temporal and parietal radiations.
Incorrect. Light reflex fibers exit the tract before the LGN to the pretectal nucleus.
items.kp: Parietal lobe lesions damage Baum loop optic radiations, causing contralateral inferior quadrantanopia (pie on the floor).

items.q: In the pupillary light reflex, afferent signals leave the optic tract before the lateral geniculate nucleus to synapse bilaterally in which midbrain structure?
items.exp: Pupillary light reflex afferent fibers branch off the optic tract to synapse in the pretectal nuclei of the rostral midbrain. Interneurons then project bilaterally to both Edinger-Westphal nuclei.
r: Correct. Afferents synapse in the pretectal nuclei to mediate bilateral pupillary constriction.
Incorrect. Superior colliculus controls visual orientation and saccades.
Incorrect. Edinger-Westphal nuclei receive secondary projections from the pretectal nuclei.
Incorrect. Ciliary ganglion contains postganglionic parasympathetic cell bodies in the orbit.
items.kp: Pupillary light reflex afferents bypass the lateral geniculate nucleus to synapse in the midbrain pretectal nuclei.

items.q: An eye clinic patient exhibits a Marcus Gunn pupil (relative afferent pupillary defect) in the right eye. Which condition is the most characteristic cause?
items.exp: A relative afferent pupillary defect (RAPD) occurs when swinging flashlight test reveals paradoxical pupillary dilation when light moves from the normal eye to the eye with damaged afferent optic nerve, classic in optic neuritis.
r: Correct. Optic neuritis causes an afferent defect manifesting as a Marcus Gunn pupil.
Incorrect. Horner syndrome is an efferent sympathetic defect.
Incorrect. CN III palsy is an efferent parasympathetic defect causing fixed mydriasis.
Incorrect. Argyll Robertson pupils accommodate but do not react to light, seen in neurosyphilis.
items.kp: Optic neuritis damages afferent pupillary signaling, producing a Marcus Gunn pupil on swinging flashlight examination.

items.q: Brodmann area 17 corresponds to which anatomical functional landmark in the occipital lobe?
o: Primary visual cortex lining calcarine sulcus
items.exp: Brodmann area 17 is the primary visual cortex (striate cortex), located along the upper and lower banks of the calcarine sulcus in the medial occipital lobe.
r: Correct. Area 17 is the striate primary visual cortex surrounding the calcarine sulcus.
Incorrect. Areas 18 and 19 represent visual association cortex.
Incorrect. Area 8 represents the frontal eye fields.
Incorrect. Parieto-occipital sulcus separates parietal and occipital lobes.
items.kp: Brodmann area 17 corresponds to primary visual (striate) cortex along the calcarine fissure.

items.q: Bilateral calcification of the internal carotid arteries impinging upon the lateral aspects of the optic chiasm can produce which rare visual field defect?
items.exp: Lateral compression of the optic chiasm damages the uncrossed temporal retinal axons from both eyes, causing loss of both nasal visual fields (binasal hemianopia).
r: Correct. Bilateral lateral chiasmal compression selectively damages uncrossed temporal retinal fibers, causing binasal hemianopia.
Incorrect. Medial central compression causes bitemporal hemianopia.
Incorrect. Unilateral tract lesions cause homonymous hemianopia.
Incorrect. Total blindness requires complete bilateral optic nerve disruption.
items.kp: Lateral chiasmal compression damages uncrossed temporal fibers, producing binasal hemianopia.
